answers_by_date.answer: Loss of employment automatically implies the loss of immigration status
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 22.439 art. 20 let the authority cancel a temporary residence 'cuando se desnaturalizaren los motivos' for which it was granted. Arts. 37–38 then provided only an order to leave or expulsion. There was no period to regularise or find a new job. Decreto 1023/94 could not be opened, and I found no practice evidence for this period.

answers_by_date.answer: Loss of employment implies loss of immigration status unless a new job is found within a specified time period
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 25.871 has been in force since 21 Jan 2004. Art. 61 obliged the DNM ('deberá conminarlo') to give an irregular migrant a deadline to regularise before expulsion. Art. 65 bars loss of residence for breach of an employment-contract obligation unless that obligation was a condition of the permit. Art. 62(d) cancels a residence whose grounds are 'desnaturalizado'. The DNM fixed the deadline case by case, since there was no regulation until 2010. I found no practice evidence on job loss itself for this period; the rating is inferred.

answers_by_date.answer: Loss of employment implies loss of immigration status unless a new job is found within a specified time period
answers_by_date.basis: Same statutory regime as in 2005. Decreto 616/2010 (May 2010) was not yet in force. The CMW's 2011 concluding observations, covering practice around 2010, found that the DNM did not weigh personal circumstances or length of stay before ordering expulsion. The Committee asked that migrants get 'adequate time to apply for residence... in accordance with article 61'.

answers_by_date.answer: Loss of employment implies loss of immigration status unless a new job is found within a specified time period
answers_by_date.basis: Decreto 616/2010 art. 61 (from May 2010): where the grounds for admission were 'desnaturalizado', the DNM must give the migrant up to 30 days to regularise, extendable by 30 more. Art. 20(a) allows a change of category. This is the starting answer's basis, unchanged until 2020; DNU 70/2017 changed art. 62 only in 2017. I found no practice source dated around 2015, so the 2020 rating is carried back.

answers.change_2000_2020: There was no right protection (as of January 1, 2000), but there is now (as of January 1, 2020)

events.what_changed: Replaced Ley 22.439. Art. 61 created a duty to give irregular migrants a deadline to regularise. Art. 65 bars loss of residence for breach of a work-contract obligation unless it was a condition of the permit. Art. 62(d) cancels a residence whose grounds are 'desnaturalizado'.

answers.notes: The 2000 answer rests on Ley 22.439 arts. 20, 37–38 (read), which give no regularisation period. Decreto 1023/94 (Reglamento de Migración) could not be opened: the InfoLEG link was dead and the ACNUR and SCBA PDFs failed. It might have contained a change-of-category rule. The 50-point answer for 2005 and 2010 rests on the art. 61 duty to give a regularisation deadline, which the DNM set itself; the length was fixed at 30+30 days only by Decreto 616/2010. ICRMW art. 51 (Ley 26.202, 2007) was not read and is not relied on. No rulings were relied on.

answers.sourcing_note: The Ley 25.871 original and current texts, Decreto 616/2010, DNU 70/2017 and Ley 22.439 were all read on InfoLEG. Decreto 1023/94 could not be read, so the 2000 answer is weaker. Practice evidence is thin: CMW 2011 for around 2010 and the CMW 2019 review via CELS; nothing for 2000, 2005 or 2015.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The citation's Decreto 616/2010 arts. 23(i) and 23(m) are unregulated or about humanitarian grounds, and do not concern job loss. The 30+30-day window in art. 61 is a general regularisation window, not a job-search period. The answer holds, but the cited articles should be corrected. The CMW (2019) also noted that self-employment was not a residence criterion, which narrows the ways to regularise after losing a dependent job.

answers.sourcing_note: The 2000 answer rests on a DNM disposition that was read. For 2005 and 2010 the continuation of the old rule is inferred from art. 124. I found no practice evidence on switching for any date.
answers.starting_answer_concern: Decreto 616 art. 22(c) lets the DNM impose further conditions by temporary-residence type. Seasonal migrant workers (art. 24(e)) are transitory, not temporary, residents and have no arraigo route. Strictly, the route therefore does depend on permit type for some temporary workers.

answers_by_date.basis: Ley de Contrato de Trabajo art. 17 bans discrimination by nationality. Art. 42 keeps a worker's right to wages and severance even when the contract has a prohibited object, which covers irregular migrants whose employment Ley 22.439 arts. 30–31 forbade. Ley 22.439 art. 104 obliged officials to report irregular residents, which likely deterred claims. I found no practice evidence for this period; the rating is inferred.

Since 21 Jan 2004, Ley 25.871 art. 56 says employers' labour obligations apply 'cualquiera sea su condición migratoria'. Arts. 16, 67 and 68 add further protection. The LCT is unchanged. I found no practice evidence specific to this period.

Same law as in 2005 (Decreto 616 art. 56 on free legal aid came in May 2010). CMW 2011 welcomed art. 56. It was concerned, however, that irregular migrant workers in textiles, agriculture and domestic work faced exploitation and that women domestic workers had 'limited access to judicial remedies'.

Ley 25.871 art. 56, Decreto 616/2010 art. 56 (free legal services may not refuse migrants for lack of documents) and LCT arts. 17 and 42. Unchanged to 2020. I found no practice source dated around 2015, so the 2020 rating is carried back.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 but they are not the same

events.what_changed: Added an explicit guarantee that employers' labour-law obligations apply whatever the worker's migration status. Under Ley 22.439, by contrast, arts. 30–31 banned work by irregular migrants and art. 104 required officials to report them.
events.passage: ARTICULO 56. — La aplicación de la presente ley no eximirá al empleador o dador de trabajo del cumplimiento de las obligaciones emergentes de la legislación laboral respecto del extranjero, cualquiera sea su condición migratoria

events.what_changed: Free legal services may not refuse migrants for lack of Argentine documents when they claim the rights in art. 56.
events.passage: los extranjeros podrán recurrir al asesoramiento que brindan los servicios jurídicos gratuitos que funcionan en el país, los cuales no podrán negarles atención debido a la falta de documentación argentina o a su calidad de extranjeros.

answers.notes: LCT arts. 17 and 42 carry no amendment notes on InfoLEG and were in force throughout 2000–2020. Ley 22.439 arts. 30, 31 and 104 were read and were in force until January 2004. No rulings were relied on. The starting answer's 'Usually' for 2020 is kept; the 2010 rating is lowered on CMW 2011 practice evidence.
